item.title: Logic Pro 13 is out: a unified browser, drum stem splitting and an AI assistant
item.description: Logic Pro 13 has been available since 5 November 2026: a unified browser with automatic sound tags, Stem Splitter for individual drum parts and the Intelligent Assistant beta. Price, requirements and what it means for mixing and mastering.

item.title: Pro Tools 2026.11 brings Extensions, a Stem Separator and MPE
item.description: Pro Tools 2026.11 introduces Extensions, a new plug-in format not tied to tracks, a local Stem Separator with up to six stems in every tier, and MPE support. Requirements and advice before you update.

item.title: Fender unveils the new American Professional and drops the II and III numbering
item.description: Fender announced the new American Professional series in October 2026, replacing the II: V-Mod III pickups, redesigned bridges, push-push tone controls and ten guitar and bass models. Left-handed versions from spring 2027.

item.title: M6 MacBook Pro and the touchscreen MacBook Pro: what matters for music
item.description: Apple launched the $1,999 M6 MacBook Pro and the first OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and M5 Max, both shipping from 6 November 2026. What to check before buying one for mixing, mastering and production.

item.title: Universal Audio takes the FATSO native: tape and compression in any DAW
item.description: Since 13 October 2026 Universal Audio’s Empirical Labs FATSO runs natively on macOS and Windows, no Apollo required. Intro price $79 until 31 December, $2.99 upgrade for owners of the DSP version.

item.title: Antares launches AutoTune Advanced: hard tuning, vibrato intact
item.description: AutoTune Advanced is Antares’ new flagship, released in late September 2026: a DVA engine that preserves vibrato, Live mode under 1 ms, $450 perpetual. How it differs from AutoTune Pro 11 and AutoTune 2026.

item.title: Audient Horizon: three Thunderbolt interfaces for pro studios, no DSP
item.description: Audient launched Horizon, three Thunderbolt 3 interfaces with 32-bit conversion, sub-millisecond latency and no proprietary DSP: Horizon 8P, 16 and 32, from $2,799 to $3,499.

item.title: iZotope moves to Boris FX: what happens to Ozone, RX and Neutron
item.description: On 2 July 2026 Boris FX acquired iZotope while inMusic completed its purchase of Native Instruments. What happens to Ozone, RX, Neutron and Nectar licences and subscriptions, and who owns what now.

item.title: Ableton Live 12.4: Link Audio, more flexible stem separation and a rebuilt Erosion
item.description: Live 12.4 is free for Live 12 owners: Link Audio streams audio in real time over the local network, stem separation works on a selection, Erosion is rebuilt, Delay gets a new LFO and there is a new Learn View.

item.title: FabFilter Pro-C 3: 14 compression styles, Character and Auto Threshold
item.description: FabFilter Pro-C 3 was released on 15 January 2026: six new styles for a total of 14, Tube, Diode and Bright Character modes, Auto Threshold, up to 32x oversampling and Atmos support up to 9.1.6.

item.title: Subtractive EQ: why cutting before boosting makes a mix breathe
item.description: How to use subtractive EQ in a mix: high-pass filters with judgement, narrow cuts on resonances, the 200 to 500 Hz zone, and when boosting is the right call.

item.title: Reverb and delay in the mix: creating space without washing it out
item.description: How to use reverb and delay on sends, filter the returns, set pre-delay and times to the BPM, and sidechain the effects so the vocal stays in front.

item.title: Saturation in mixing and mastering: warmth, density and when to stop
item.description: Types of saturation (tape, tube, transformer, clipper), where to use them in the mix and the master, how to set them at matched loudness and the signs you are overdoing it.

item.title: Mix bus compression: a tutorial for gluing the track together
item.description: How to set up a mix bus compressor: ratio, attack, release, sidechain filter and how much gain reduction it takes to glue a track without squashing it.

item.title: De-essing vocals: a tutorial for clear vocals without harsh esses
item.description: How to find the sibilance frequency, set the de-esser, when to use split-band or wideband mode, and how to fix the harshest esses by hand.

item.title: The mastering limiter: a tutorial for loudness without distortion
item.description: How to set a mastering limiter: true peak ceiling at −0.3/−0.2 dBTP, oversampling, attack and release, how much gain reduction is safe and how to check the result.

item.title: Mid/side EQ in mastering: widen and clean up without losing the centre
item.description: What mid/side EQ is, how to use it in mastering to clean the low end on the sides, add air to the stereo image and bring the vocal forward, and the limits that keep mono safe.

item.title: Reference tracks: how to actually use them in mixing and mastering
item.description: How to choose references, match loudness before comparing, what to listen for (low end, vocal, stereo, dynamics) and the mistakes that make you copy the wrong song.

item.title: Afro house mastering: percussion, low end and club loudness
item.description: How I master an afro house track: percussion that stays alive, a tight mono low end, vocals and ethnic instruments in their place, loudness for Beatport and streaming.

item.title: Master delivery formats: bit depth, sample rate, dither and metadata
item.description: Which format a master needs for distribution: 24-bit WAV, sample rate, when to dither, file naming, ISRC codes and the checks to make before uploading.

item.title: LUFS and streaming in 2026: what platforms do to your master
item.description: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Tidal, Amazon Music and Deezer: the 2026 normalization levels and what they really mean for the loudness of your master.

item.title: Gain staging in your DAW: a step-by-step tutorial for a clean mix
item.description: How to set levels in your DAW from recording to the master bus: clip gain, plugins calibrated to −18 dBFS, headroom for mastering. A tutorial with practical values.

item.title: Mixing vs mastering: who does what, and when you need each
item.description: Mixing and mastering explained without jargon: what happens in each stage, what mastering cannot fix and when stem mastering is the smarter choice.

item.title: Vocal compression: a tutorial with two compressors in series
item.description: How to compress vocals in the mix: clip gain, a fast compressor on the peaks, an optical one for cohesion, de-esser and automation. With practical starting values.

item.title: True peak: why −1 dBTP is not a rule, and what I check instead
item.description: What true peak is, where the −1 dBTP advice comes from, why I deliver at −0.3/−0.2 dBTP with a true peak limiter and how to check the file after encoding.

item.title: How to export tracks for mixing and mastering: Ableton, FL Studio, Logic, Pro Tools and Cubase
item.description: How to prepare and export tracks, stems and premasters: formats, start point, effect tails, naming. For Ableton, FL Studio, Logic, Pro Tools and Cubase.

item.title: Mixing rap and trap vocals with Auto-Tune: the chain I use
item.description: How to mix rap and trap vocals with Auto-Tune: tuning as an effect, clean-up, firm compression, saturation, ad-libs and tempo-synced delays. Examples and practical values.

item.title: Tuning the kick and 808 to the key of the track: step-by-step tutorial
item.description: How to find the pitch of your kick and 808, tune them to the root or the fifth and avoid cancellation between the two. With a frequency table.

item.title: Analog mastering: what SSL Fusion, API 2500, tape and Pultec really do
item.description: What analog gear adds to mastering, when it helps and when it does not: SSL Fusion, API 2500, tape and Pultec-style EQ inside a hybrid chain.

item.title: Phase and mono compatibility: a tutorial for a mix that holds up everywhere
item.description: How to check phase and mono compatibility in the mix: correlation, mic polarity, kick layers, wideners, mono lows and a band-by-band check.

item.title: Depth in the mix: how to give a track three dimensions
item.description: How to build depth in the mix: level, high frequencies, transients, pre-delay, early reflections and the contrast between dry and wet elements. With a practical method.

item.title: Mixing on headphones: how to get a mix that also works on speakers
item.description: The limits of headphones in mixing and how to get past them: open-back headphones, correction, crossfeed, matched-level references and checks on other systems.

item.title: Premaster mistakes that make mastering worse, and how to avoid them
item.description: A limiter on the master, clipping, normalization, MP3s, cut-off tails, wideners on the bus: the most common mistakes in files sent for mastering and how to fix them.

item.title: How much to spend on a home studio: where money matters and where it does not
item.description: Budgeting a home studio: in what order to spend, why returns flatten out above 8–9 thousand dollars and when it makes sense to go beyond 40 thousand.

item.title: How to choose a mixing and mastering engineer: the right questions to ask
item.description: How to choose a mixing and mastering engineer, online or in a studio: work in your genre, reviews, revisions, delivery formats, turnaround, clear prices and communication.

item.title: LUFS Explained: The Only Loudness Guide Producers Need
item.description: Integrated, short-term, momentary, LRA, true peak: what each number actually measures, what streaming platforms do with them, and the targets that matter in 2026.

item.title: How Loud Should Your Master Be in 2026? Streaming vs Club
item.description: Stop chasing -14 LUFS. The real loudness strategy depends on where your track lives: playlists, clubs, or both. Here are the numbers working engineers actually target.

item.title: Hybrid vs Full ITB: What Actually Matters for Your Master
item.description: Analog gear or plugins? After 15 years of running both, here is where hybrid mastering genuinely wins, where it does not, and how to tell if your track needs it.

item.title: Low-End in Melodic Techno: The Techniques That Actually Work
item.description: Kick and bass are 80% of a melodic techno record. Here is the exact framework I use to make the low end huge, clean and club-translatable — sidechain, mono, tuning and headroom.

item.title: Mixing Vocals for Pop and RnB: Air, Presence and Pocket
item.description: The lead vocal is the record in pop and RnB. My chain and philosophy for vocals that sit on top of dense productions without shouting: gain riding, serial compression, air EQ and the pocket.

item.title: The Camelot Wheel: Harmonic Mixing for Producers and DJs
item.description: 8A mixes with 7A, 9A and 8B — and knowing why makes you a better producer, not just a better DJ. The Camelot system explained, with the shortcuts that matter.

item.title: How to Prepare Your Stems for a Professional Mix
item.description: Badly prepared stems cost you revisions, time and quality. The exact export checklist I send my clients: formats, labeling, gain staging, and the five mistakes that delay every project.

item.title: Apple Digital Masters: What It Actually Means for Your Music

item.description: Clubs don't normalize; streaming does. Whether your electronic release needs separate club and streaming masters, and how I decide — with the loudness numbers for each destination.
